description: Seventy-five to a hundred solar panels caught fire on the roof of an Amazon fulfillment center in West Jefferson, Ohio. The fifth massive fire in five days.

faqs.answer: The official cause is under investigation, but fire officials believe 75-100 solar panels on the roof caught fire. Jefferson Township Fire Chief Dan Gatley stated they are in the early stages of determining the exact cause.
faqs.question: What caused the Amazon warehouse fire in Ohio?

faqs.answer: No. The fire department reported no injuries. Thousands of employees were evacuated as a precaution and sent home for the rest of the day.
faqs.question: Was anyone injured in the West Jefferson Amazon fire?

faqs.answer: Jefferson Township Fire Chief Dan Gatley estimated that 75-100 solar panels on the roof caught fire. The fire was contained to the roof area.
faqs.question: How many solar panels caught fire?

faqs.answer: Fire damage was minimal. Chief Gatley reported the fire burned through a small section of the rubber roofing membrane and some insulation, affecting approximately two racks of product. Most of the damage was from water and the sprinkler system.
faqs.question: What was the damage to the Amazon facility?

faqs.answer: The fire was reported at 12:10 PM on April 8, 2026. Fire crews confirmed the fire on the roof and began battling it immediately. The fire was contained, and employees were evacuated and sent home for the day.
faqs.question: How long did it take to contain the fire?

faqs.answer: Multiple agencies responded, led by the Jefferson Township Fire Department. Approximately 10 fire engines responded along with mutual aid from nearby departments, including Madison Township and Pleasant Township fire departments.
faqs.question: Which fire departments responded?
